Use image 1 as the ground grass texture to replace completely, and image 2 ONLY as the visual style and palette reference. Create the replacement square seamless repeating grass albedo texture for a stylized top-down 3D puzzle game.

Match the olive yellow-green mossy ground on the platform TOPS in the screenshot: a predominantly smooth, matte, warm muted olive grass carpet, soft broad angular painted color facets, gently mottled patches, a few tiny loose clusters of rounded moss nodules and very sparse short grass strokes. The grass reads as simplified mossy turf, not photorealistic long blades. Keep 90 percent of the surface quiet and flat. Palette around ochre olive #96943c and #a1a345, with restrained darker olive and pale yellow-green accents. No saturated emerald green, no dark forest-green areas.

Production requirements: one full-bleed square texture, 1024 x 1024 pixels, opaque RGB. Camera exactly orthographic overhead; surface lies flat across the entire image. Seamlessly tile both horizontally and vertically with matching opposite edges and continuous markings. All four corners match. Evenly distributed texture density, no border, no empty margins, no central subject. This image repeats once per four ground tiles, so details should remain legible but sparse. Hand-painted flat-shaded low-poly fantasy game surface, broad soft polygonal brush marks, restrained contrast and clean simplified shapes.

Do not include any part of the screenshot scene: no stone slabs, no cliff edges or cliff sides, no islands, no sky, no fog, no characters, no objects, no lighting gradient, no perspective, no directional shadows, no text. This is only a reusable olive moss-grass surface texture.

Use image 1 as the ground rock texture to replace completely, and image 2 ONLY as the visual style and palette reference. Create the replacement square seamless repeating STONE albedo texture for a stylized top-down 3D puzzle game.

Match the pale warm creamy sandstone/limestone on the platform TOPS in the screenshot. A continuous matte bedrock surface broken into broad irregular polygonal stone plates with subtle angular faces, shallow thin meandering hairline cracks and softly chipped edges. Predominantly warm sandy cream #d4c69d, pale beige #c7b78d and restrained ivory edge accents. Closely fitted plates form a continuous natural rock floor, not loose paving stones. The thin irregular fissures have understated taupe shading and occasional delicate pale highlights; no black crevices or heavy outlines. Broad quiet flat surfaces, subtle hand-painted uneven wear, occasional tiny pale stone chips. Simplified low-poly fantasy game material matching the reference. No moss or grass in this stone texture, as it will blend over a separate olive grass texture.

Production requirements: one full-bleed square texture, 1024 x 1024 pixels, opaque RGB. Camera exactly orthographic overhead; surface lies flat across the entire image. Seamlessly tile both horizontally and vertically with matching opposite edges, continuous crack markings at edges, and matching corners. Every edge must visually connect to its opposite. Even detail density, no border, no empty margins, no central focal point. One texture spans four by four board tiles, with roughly 25 to 35 irregular broad plates of varied size across the square, so the delicate cracks remain readable in-game. Albedo only, soft restrained contrast, even neutral illumination.

Exclude the screenshot scene: no cliff faces, no sides, no islands, no sky, no fog, no characters, no large separate stones, no objects, no perspective, no directional cast shadows, no baked lighting gradient, no text. Avoid photorealistic grain, pixel art, cobblestones, regular brick grids, orange rock, cool dark gray stone, and deep black cracks. This is only a reusable pale warm natural cracked stone surface texture.
